title: Indirection: Flank, Wedge, Long Maneuver

keyConcepts.name: Divide-and-conquer (wedge)
keyConcepts.description: Finding the genuine divergence of interest within an opposing coalition, amplifying it, and attacking the fragmented pieces separately. Requires accurate intelligence about where the real seam is. Clumsy wedge attempts produce solidarity rather than fracture.

keyConcepts.name: Flank attack
keyConcepts.description: Attacking the soft, unprepared side rather than the strong defended front. Cheaper and faster because the flank is less defended; the opponent's response to a flank attack also degrades their frontal defense. Requires reconnaissance to find the flank and recognition of when no flank exists.

keyConcepts.name: Ripening (long maneuver)
keyConcepts.description: Removing the conditions that sustain the opponent's position rather than attacking it directly. The opponent moves themselves into collapse when their options have all been removed. Requires patience and secrecy; fails if either is lost.

connectingThread: Three indirection disciplines that require no direct force: divide what is united, attack the undefended side, remove what the opponent needs and wait. All three require more patience and more accurate intelligence than direct attack, and all produce more efficient outcomes when they work. All three have a legitimate form (using real information and real situations) and a manipulative form (using fabrication or coercion).

callbackOpportunities.concept: Intelligence (Strategy 13) is the prerequisite for divide-and-conquer (must know where the real seam is) and for flank attack (must identify where the real flank is). Without Ch5 intelligence work, both strategies target the wrong seam or the wrong flank.

Ripening connects back to Ch3's nonengagement discipline: both are patience-based strategies that trade time for position. The difference is that nonengagement is defensive (trading ground to survive), while ripening is offensive (removing conditions to produce the opponent's collapse).

reversalFlags.flag: Clumsy or obvious wedge attempts unite the coalition around their shared interest. The strategy requires delicacy and genuine intelligence about the seam -- a missed seam or an obvious manipulation attempt backfires.
Some positions have no soft flank. Prolonged search for a non-existent flank costs initiative. The discipline includes recognizing when the direct attack is the only viable option.

Requires simultaneous patience and secrecy. If the operator acts too early, the opponent is still in a position to resist. If the opponent discovers the long maneuver, the strategy converts into a direct confrontation the operator was not ready for.

moralFlagNote: Every indirect move has a legitimate form (strategic use of real information and real divergences) and a manipulative form (fabrication, manufactured conflict, coercive interference). The hard breakdown must name the ethical line explicitly for each strategy.
